text: A spiked iron door slams shut. The iron maiden, the most famous torture device of the Middle Ages.
Except there's no proof one existed before the 1800s.
In 1793, a German writer claimed one killed a coin forger in 1515.
That's almost 300 years later, with no record to back it up.
Then one was likely pieced together from old museum parts and shown off in Nuremberg.
A copy even toured America after the 1893 Chicago World's Fair.
Good news: nobody in the Middle Ages died in one.
Bad news: in 2003, reporters in Baghdad found a real one, at Olympic offices run by Saddam Hussein's son.
